article_title: Unmasked ICE agents hounded at airports: "Nazis don't belong"
article_content:
Federal immigration agents assisting security operations at major U.S. airports have been confronted by travelers, including at least one who accused them of being "Nazis."
Video shared on social media shows a woman shouting at Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) personnel at Newark International Liberty Airport, saying: "Nazis don't belong in America and they don't belong in airports."
Why It Matters
The confrontation comes after President Donald Trump's administration sent hundreds of ICE agents to airports nationwide to help manage operational strain linked to Transportation Security Administration (TSA) staffing shortages.
The disruption stems from a partial Department of Homeland Security (DHS) shutdown that began on February 14, leaving tens of thousands of TSA officers working without pay and contributing to widespread callouts and resignations, worsening delays at airports across the country. The DHS has said that around 400 TSA officers had left the force since the shutdown.
In response, ICE agents have been deployed to at least 14 airports to assist with crowd control, line management, and securing exit areas. The move has drawn criticism as the officers are primarily trained for immigration enforcement rather than aviation security.
DHS oversees federal agencies such as TSA and ICE.
What To Know
The woman in the video circulating on social media could be heard shouting at agents across a baggage claim, telling them to "go back to your master, Donald Trump," footage shows.
She was also seen shouting "ICE out now" at agents. Footage also shows ICE agents standing idle at Newark Liberty International Airport, with video capturing them observing but not engaging with travelers.
Homeland Security Investigations agents, which is a subdivision of ICE, were being deployed to 14 airports, including New York’s JFK, Cleveland, Pittsburgh, Phoenix, Fort Myers, Atlanta and Chicago’s O’Hare airports, according to officials and social media footage.
At Chicago O’Hare International Airport, Mayor Brandon Johnson told Newsweek that about 75 ICE officers were expected to be deployed across multiple shifts beginning Monday, March 23.
Officials have said the agents are assigned to support roles such as crowd management and logistical coordination, rather than primary screening duties.
President Donald Trump said Monday in a Truth Social post he does not support allowing ICE agents to wear masks while assisting at airports.
Trump told reporters on Monday: "I actually suggested that the airports, they take off their masks and they did that…I didn't love the look in the airport as you get off the plane. So, I made a request and they agreed to it."
Lawmakers from both parties have blamed each other over the shutdown as spring break travel faces widespread disruptions. Some Democratic senators have withheld support for a funding package, citing the recent deaths of two U.S. citizens during a major enforcement operation in Minneapolis and calling for agency reforms before approving additional resources.
Meanwhile, Markwayne Mullin has been confirmed as the new Secretary of Homeland Security following the ouster of Kristi Noem. The U.S. Senate voted 54—45 to confirm Mullin as Secretary of Homeland Security, with most Republicans voting in favor. Two Democratic senators, John Fetterman of Pennsylvania and Martin Heinrich of New Mexico, also voted to confirm, while Republican Rand Paul voted against the nomination.
What People Are Saying
Former ICE Baltimore Field Office Director Darius Reeves, who retired last year, told Newsweek: "I believe it's a provocative move from the administration…you're politicizing once again…a law enforcement entity."
Lauren Bis, a spokesperson for DHS, told Newsweek, "While the Democrats continue to put the safety, dependability, and ease of our air travel at risk, President Trump is taking action to deploy hundreds of ICE officers, that are currently funded by Congress, to airports being adversely impacted. This will help bolster TSA efforts to keep our skies safe and minimize air travel disruptions."
President Donald Trump said Monday in a Truth Social post: "I am a BIG proponent of ICE wearing masks as they search for, and are forced to deal with, hardened criminals, many of whom were let into our Country by Sleepy Joe Biden and his wonderful 'Border Czar,' Kamala (she never even went to the Border!), through their absolutely INSANE Open Border Policy. I would greatly appreciate, however, NO MASKS, when helping our Country out of the Democrat caused MESS at the airports, etc."
What Happens Next
Congressional talks on DHS funding between both sides of the aisle showed little visible progress. Trump has urged lawmakers to stay in Washington over the Easter recess.
